summary: Configured `/srv/reports` on node1. Members of `report-writers` can create, modify, and delete content; `report-readers` can list and read but cannot create, modify, or delete. Default ACLs enforce the same policy on new content. Configuration survived the mandatory node restart.
actions_performed: Applied access and default ACLs granting writers read/write access, readers read-only access, and no access to others.
Validated permissions using distinct unprivileged identities.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified its boot identity changed.
Verified ACLs, data checksums, and effective permissions after restart.

evidence.requirement: Groups and persistent directory ACL configuration
evidence.summary: Shows both groups and the directory's ownership, setgid mode, access ACL, and default inherited ACL.

evidence.requirement: Writers can modify contents and readers have read-only access
evidence.summary: Direct tests show writer create/modify/delete succeeds while reader list/read succeeds and reader append/create/delete is denied. Final proof shows the directory clean after test-artifact removal.

Shows the healthy pre-restart filesystem, ACL, data and access baseline; safe reboot acknowledgement; boot ID changing from 5fb1b173-c1c8-4647-b118-0145511f0fcc to 406892c0-b13e-4fa4-8d08-41df3bf162fc; and recovered ACLs, matching checksums, groups, filesystem, and effective permissions.
